my elderly mother takes her blood pressure medication only when she feels dizzy and skips it on days when she feels fine is that dangerous or does it not matter if her blood pressure seems normal

Yes, this is very dangerous. High blood pressure medication must be taken every single day as prescribed, not just when symptoms appear.  Blood pressure medicine works to prevent blood pressure from rising to dangerous levels. Skipping doses causes blood pressure to spike and fall, which puts a great strain on the heart and blood vessels, increasing the risk of a stroke or heart attack. High blood pressure is often called the "silent killer" because it usually has no symptoms, so feeling "fine" does not mean her blood pressure is normal.  The dizziness itself is a concern. It could be a symptom of very high blood pressure, or it could be a side effect of the medication causing her pressure to go too low. She should take her medicine every day and speak with her doctor about the dizziness. The doctor may need to adjust her dose or change the medication.

my kid started amoxicillin for an ear infection and now she has a rash all over her body is this an allergy or is it that rash that happens with certain viruses

This is a common and confusing situation. There are two main possibilities, as you suspected. A true amoxicillin allergy often causes hives (itchy, raised welts that can move around the body), swelling of the lips or face, and can happen soon after taking the medicine. The other possibility is a delayed, non-allergic rash of flat pink spots that often appears 5-7 days after starting amoxicillin, especially if the underlying illness was viral.  You must have a doctor look at the rash to know for sure. Contact the doctor who prescribed the amoxicillin and describe the rash to them; they may want to see a photo or have you come in.  **Go to the hospital immediately** if your child develops any trouble breathing, wheezing, or swelling of the face, lips, or tongue. These are signs of a severe allergic reaction. Otherwise, stop the medication and call your doctor for guidance.

how do I talk to my 8-year-old about why they need to see a therapist without making them feel broken

It's wise to approach this conversation with care and honesty. You can explain that a therapist is like a "feelings coach" or a "feelings doctor" who helps people understand and manage big emotions like anger, sadness, or worry. Frame it as learning a new skill, just like learning to play a sport or an instrument. Reassure them that many kids and adults see therapists to learn helpful tools, and it doesn't mean anything is wrong with them. You could say, "We're going to meet someone who can help us learn new ways to handle those big feelings you've been having." This makes it a team effort and focuses on building strength, not fixing a problem.

every time I stand up quickly I see stars and nearly black out and my blood pressure sitting is fine but when I stand it drops to like 80 over 50

This is a classic sign of orthostatic hypotension, which is a drop in blood pressure when you stand up. When you stand, gravity pulls blood down into your legs, and for a moment, not enough blood gets to your brain, causing the dizziness and vision changes. The most important thing you can do is to stand up slowly, giving your body time to adjust. Sit on the edge of your bed or chair for a minute before you stand up completely.  Staying well-hydrated by drinking plenty of water is also very important, as dehydration can make this much worse. Before you stand, try pumping your ankles or clenching your leg muscles to help push blood back up toward your heart. If you ever actually faint and fall, if it is accompanied by chest pain, or if this is a new or worsening problem, you should see a doctor to check for any underlying causes.

Він допомагає зняти напругу в м'язах шиї, плечей та голови, яка часто є тригером або посилює мігренозний біль. Також масаж знижує рівень стресу — одного з найпоширеніших провокаторів нападів. Однак, під час гострого нападу мігрені масаж може погіршити стан через підвищену чутливість до дотиків, тому його краще застосовувати між нападами. Обговоріть зі своїм лікарем, чи підходить вам цей метод як частина комплексного лікування.

This is a medical emergency. You need to take your child to the nearest hospital emergency department immediately. Please go now; time is very important.

my dog bit a neighbor kid not deep but broke the skin what first aid should I do and do they need to see a doctor

First, immediately wash the wound gently but thoroughly with mild soap and running water for several minutes to clean it well. Apply pressure with a clean cloth to stop any bleeding and then cover it with a sterile bandage.  Yes, the child must see a doctor, even if the bite seems minor. Any bite that breaks the skin carries a high risk of serious infection from bacteria in the dog's mouth. A doctor will properly clean the wound, decide if antibiotics are needed, and check the child's tetanus vaccination status. Be prepared to provide your dog's vaccination records, as the doctor will need to assess the risk for rabies.

I've been fainting a few times a week for the past month and it happens without warning even when I'm sitting down

Fainting multiple times a week, especially without warning and while sitting, is a serious concern that requires immediate medical attention. This pattern suggests the cause may not be a simple faint and could be related to your heart's rhythm, blood pressure regulation, or another underlying medical condition. You need to be evaluated by a doctor as soon as possible. Given the frequency and lack of warning, going to an emergency department for a thorough evaluation is the safest course of action. They will likely perform an electrocardiogram (ECG) to check your heart's electrical activity and other tests to find the cause. Until you are evaluated, avoid activities where fainting could be dangerous, such as driving, operating machinery, or swimming.

I heard you should never take ibuprofen on an empty stomach is that really dangerous or just uncomfortable

It is more than just uncomfortable; it can be dangerous over time. Ibuprofen can irritate the lining of your stomach, and taking it without food increases this risk. This irritation can lead to stomach pain, heartburn, and in more serious or long-term cases, ulcers or bleeding. Food acts as a buffer, helping to protect your stomach. Always try to take ibuprofen with a meal or at least a glass of milk. If you experience severe stomach pain, vomiting, or black, tarry stools after taking it, you should seek medical help immediately.

our 16 year old was diagnosed with Graves' disease and now she's shaking and her heart rate is super fast is this a thyroid crisis

Yes, these symptoms could be signs of a thyroid storm, which is a life-threatening medical emergency. A thyroid storm is an extreme form of hyperthyroidism where the body is overwhelmed by a large amount of thyroid hormone. Key signs are a very high heart rate (often over 140 beats per minute), severe shaking, high fever, agitation, or confusion.  Do not wait. You need to take her to the nearest hospital emergency department immediately or call for an ambulance. This condition requires urgent medical treatment to bring her heart rate and hormone levels down safely. Tell the medical staff that she has Graves' disease and you are concerned about a thyroid storm.

my friend with bipolar disorder stopped her meds because she felt great and says she doesn't need them anymore

This is a very common but dangerous situation. The medications for bipolar disorder are meant to keep mood stable and prevent future episodes, not just treat current ones. Stopping them suddenly, especially when feeling good, can trigger a relapse into either severe depression or a manic episode.  Feeling great is wonderful, but in bipolar disorder, this can sometimes be the beginning of a manic episode where judgment is impaired. It is crucial that your friend does not change her treatment plan on her own. Encourage her to speak with her doctor immediately to discuss how she's feeling and create a safe plan together.  Watch for warning signs of mania, such as decreased need for sleep, talking very fast, racing thoughts, or impulsive, risky behavior. If you see these signs or are worried for her immediate safety, you may need to seek emergency medical help.

This is a life-threatening medical emergency called High-Altitude Pulmonary Edema (HAPE), which is fluid building up in the lungs. The pink, frothy sputum is a classic sign of this condition. Her confusion and poor coordination also suggest a related condition, High-Altitude Cerebral Edema (HACE), where the brain swells. She must be taken to the nearest hospital immediately for oxygen and specialized treatment. While waiting for transport, keep her sitting upright to make breathing easier.

my daughter has sickle cell and she's 30 weeks pregnant and her doctor said her spleen might be enlarging what does that mean

In people with sickle cell disease, the spleen's job of filtering blood can be difficult. Sometimes, a large number of sickled red blood cells get trapped in the spleen, causing it to swell with blood. This is called splenic sequestration.  This is a serious condition because it traps a lot of blood, leading to a sudden and dangerous drop in blood count (severe anemia). Your daughter's doctor is monitoring for this because pregnancy can increase the risk.  Watch for these warning signs: sudden weakness, looking unusually pale, a fast heartbeat, feeling dizzy, or having new pain on the upper left side of her belly.  If any of these symptoms appear, this is a medical emergency. You must go to the hospital immediately. Her doctors are aware of the risk and will be prepared to treat her quickly.

Symptoms can include nausea, vomiting, weakness, frequent urination, and bone pain. Over time, it can lead to serious problems like kidney stones and damage to your heart and blood vessels. It is best to have your vitamin D levels checked by a doctor who can recommend the correct dose for you based on a blood test.

Effective pain management often involves treating both the physical source of the pain and the psychological responses to it through methods like physical therapy, medication, and cognitive-behavioral therapy.
